title: Unsupervised expression subtypes differ in measured lung function in pulmonary fibrosis
summary: Consensus clustering of oxidative-stress-related expression profiles identified pulmonary-fibrosis subgroups with different measured respiratory function and symptom scores. Primary Figure1 shows subtypeB with better FVC, DLCO and respiratory quality-of-life scores, despite its higher computed oxidative-stress score. This direction conflicts with the abstract narrative, so the result is retained only as a retrospective subtype association, without causal or treatment claims.
ai_technology: Unsupervised consensus clustering of gene-expression profiles; LASSO, random forests and SVM-RFE for ancillary marker selection

evidence.tested: The primary Methods used GSE32537 as the training dataset and ConsensusClusterPlus to learn two subgroups from154 oxidative-stress-related genes. Figure1H–J and main Results associate subtypeB with lower StGeorge respiratory-questionnaire scores and higher percent-predicted FVC and DLCO than subtypeA. These are measured patient characteristics rather than clustering-separation benchmarks.
evidence.unknown: The abstract implies better respiratory status at lower oxidative-stress scores, whereas Figure1F/H–J and main Results show better function in the subgroup with higher computed scores. The biological direction is unresolved and is not adopted. The clustering relationship is retrospective; reproducible clinical subtype assignment, causal mechanisms, antioxidant treatment benefit and prospective utility are unestablished. Ancillary animal and drug claims are not independently adjudicated.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised consensus learning defined expression-based patient subgroups whose association with measured respiratory function constitutes the represented clinical finding. PCA separation alone and biomarker classification benchmarks are not treated as discoveries.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary PMC cohort/consensus-clustering and marker-selection Methods, respiratory-function and clinical subgroup Results; directly viewed primary Figure1 to verify direction. Publisher canonical front metadata and fresh PubMed relationships checked. Operational animal/cell procedures, drug effects and supplementary implementation not adjudicated. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
